East Kilbride is a thriving area with strong demand for reliable full bathroom installation and fitting services. Local properties range from period Victorian and Edwardian homes through to modern new-build developments, each presenting different plumbing requirements and challenges.

Our Gas Safe registered engineers serve all areas of East Kilbride and the surrounding South Lanarkshire region. Whether you're in the town centre or the surrounding residential areas, we provide prompt, professional bathroom installation services with transparent pricing and no hidden call-out charges.

With years of experience working across South Lanarkshire, our engineers understand the specific plumbing challenges faced by local homeowners. From the older pipe infrastructure common in period properties to the modern systems found in newer developments, our team has the expertise to handle any full bathroom installation and fitting requirement.

We cover all postcodes across East Kilbride with same-day availability for urgent work. All our engineers are fully qualified, insured, and committed to leaving your property clean and tidy after every job.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for a new bathroom?
faqs.a: In most cases, no. Replacing like-for-like or fitting a new bathroom within existing walls does not require planning permission. Moving soil stacks or creating a new bathroom in unconverted space may require Building Regulations approval.

faqs.q: Can you move the toilet and bath to different positions?
faqs.a: Yes, but it depends on the soil pipe route and floor structure. Moving a toilet more than a metre from the existing soil stack requires a new soil pipe connection and increases cost significantly.

faqs.q: How much does a bathroom installation cost?
faqs.a: Labour for a full bathroom installation typically ranges from £2,500 to £5,000 depending on complexity. Suite and tile costs are separate. A complete bathroom renovation including all materials typically costs £4,000 to £10,000+.

faqs.q: Should I supply my own bathroom suite or let the plumber supply it?
faqs.a: You can do either. Supplying your own suite gives you more choice and control over the brand and style. Your installer may offer trade discounts worth 15-30% off RRP if they supply.

localParagraph: Bathroom installation across East Kilbride presents a varied and interesting challenge for homeowners, given the town's mix of post-war council properties, 1970s new town developments, and more recent private builds spread across neighbourhoods such as St Leonards, Westwood, and Hairmyres. South Lanarkshire's water supply in this part of Scotland falls into a mixed hardness category, meaning some properties experience moderate limescale accumulation around taps, shower heads, and seals over time — a factor that experienced local installers will account for when recommending fixtures, sealants, and pipe fittings designed for longevity. The variety of property ages in East Kilbride also means that plumbing configurations, wall constructions, and floor substrates can differ significantly from one street to the next, making a proper survey essential before any installation begins. Whether you are upgrading a bathroom in a 1960s semi-detached in Calderwood or fitting an entirely new wet room in a modern apartment closer to the town centre, working with a contractor who understands the specific conditions of this area will help ensure a durable and well-finished result.
whatItInvolves: A full bathroom installation covers everything from stripping out the existing suite to fitting the new one — including all pipework, waste connections, tiling preparation, flooring, and electrical work for lighting and extraction. A quality bathroom installation transforms one of the most-used rooms in your home and typically adds 3-5% to your property value.
process: The process starts with a detailed survey to assess existing pipework, drainage routes, and structural considerations. Day 1-2: strip out and prep. Day 3-4: first fix plumbing and any structural work. Day 5-7: suite installation, tiling, and second fix. Day 8-10: finishing, sealant, and final inspection. You'll be without a working bathroom for 5-10 days depending on complexity — we'll agree a realistic timeline upfront.
whatToExpect: Expect a detailed written quote covering labour, waste disposal, and any structural work. Suite and tiles are usually supplied separately by you or sourced through us. All plumbing work is carried out to Water Regulations standards. A bathroom installation is a major investment — ask to see previous work and Gas Safe registration before committing to any installer.
